questions.question: In economics, IPO stands for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Initial Public offering.__**

__
 
• **Initial public offering**__** (IPO) **is the process by which a private company can go public by sale of its stocks to the general public.
 
• It could be a new, young company or an old company which decides to be listed on an exchange and hence goes public.
 
• Companies can raise equity capital with the help of an IPO by issuing new shares to the public or the existing shareholders can sell their shares to the public without raising any fresh capital.
 
• The company which offers its shares, known as an** 'issuer'.**

questions.question: When is World Hypertension Day celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __17th May.__**

__
 
• Every year, **17 May**__ is dedicated to** World Hypertension Day **(WHD).
 
• The** theme** for World Hypertension Day is **Know Your Numbers** with a goal of increasing high blood pressure (BP) awareness in all populations around the world.
 
• This is an initiative of the **World Hypertension League** (WHL), an affiliated section of the International Society of Hypertension.
 
• The WHD was first inaugurated in May 2005 and has become an annual event ever since.
 
• The purpose of the WHD is to promote **public awareness of hypertension **and to encourage citizens of all countries to prevent and control this **silent killer**, the modern epidemic.

questions.question: The book 'Delhi is not far' is written by which of the following authors?

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India provisions for reservations of seats for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes in the House of People?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e.__ Article 330.__

__

• __**Article 335**__ provides for the claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to services and posts

questions.question: Who was the first woman to become the governor of an Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Sarojini Naidu.__**

__

• She was born on February 13, 1879, in Hyderabad.
 
• She was a political activist, feminist, and poet.
 
• She was the **first Indian woman** to be president of the Indian National Congress
 
• She was called “**the Nightingale of India**” or "**Bharatiya Kokila**".
 
• She died on March 2, 1949, Lucknow.

questions.question: In which year was the Chicago (USA) Conference of World Religions held that included Swami Vivekananda's talk on religion as one of its highlights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4) i.e. __1893__.**

__
 
• The **1893 **__World’s Parliament of Religions was held on the shore of **Lake Michigan, Chicago **was the largest and most spectacular event among many other congresses.
 
• The World Congress of Religions marks the first formal gathering of representatives of Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda** mesmerized the 5,000 assembled delegates, greeting them with the words, **“Sisters and brothers of America!” **
 
• This speech, which introduced** Hinduism to America** is memorized by school children in India to this day.
 
• Swami Vivekananda became one of the most forceful and popular speakers in spite of the fact that he had never before addressed an audience in public.
 
• 19 women spoke at this Parliament, an unprecedented occurrence until 1893.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. __Marie Curie.__**

__
 
• The first woman to win a Nobel Prize was **Marie Curie**__, who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 with her husband, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel.
 
• Together with her husband, Pierre, she discovered radium, an element widely used for treating cancer and studied uranium and other radioactive substances
 
• In 1911, she won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the isolation of radium.
 
• Curie is also the only woman to have won multiple Nobel Prizes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays a role in blood clotting, bone metabolism and regulating blood calcium levels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3) i.e. __Vitamin K.__**

 
• Vitamin K (**Phylloquinone**) is a vitamin found in** leafy green vegetables, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts.**
 
• In the body, vitamin K plays a major role in blood clotting. So it is used to reverse the effects of “blood-thinning” medications when too much is given

questions.question: For economists, ________ refers to the amount of a product or service that people are both willing and able to buy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Demand.__**

 
• **Demand **in economics is defined as consumers' willingness and ability to consume a given good.
 
• **Supply** in economics is defined as the total amount of a specific good or service that is available to consumers.
 
• The** law of demand** says that at higher prices, buyers will demand less of an economic good.
 
• The** law of supply** says that at higher prices, sellers will supply more of an economic good.

questions.question: ________ is the smallest unit of data in a computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Bit.__**

__
 
• A** bit__ **is a binary digit and it is the **smallest** unit of data on a computer.
 
• A** **__**bit**__ can hold only one of two values:** 0 or 1.**
 
• Bits are usually assembled into a group of eight to form a byte.
 
• 1 Kilobyte = 1024 Bytes.
 
• 1 Megabyte = 1024 Kilobytes.
 
• 1 Gigabyte = 1024 Megabytes.
 
• 1 Terabyte = 1024 Gigabytes.
